"W-what...? Wh-why on earth are you thinking about that now?" As she rolled her eyes in flustered surprise, Harry offered her a gentle, affectionate smile.

Harry found her with a speed incomparable to any moment in his life.
In malfoyd's sweat-drenched, exhausted embrace rested a treasure worth more than anything in the world.

"It's a daughter, Potter."

In Harry's eyes, two jewels were shining: the child to whom he would dedicate his entire life, and the beautiful girl who had already sworn to give him everything she was.

"Her hair is blonde. She takes after her mother."

At those words, she smiled through her exhaustion and replied,

"Her eyes take after you."

The baby was lovely, but Harry could only feel a deep sense of heartache, looking at malfoyd's tired, thin face from all she had been through.
Pressing a gentle kiss to her forehead, Harry proudly took in both her and their child within a single gaze.

"I’ll spend the rest of my life making up for every single drop of sweat you shed and every hardship you endured. Even now, you look far more dazzling and beautiful to me than when I first fell in love with you."

She smiled with a mixture of contentment and playful teasing, looking up at him warmly.

"Stupid Potter, you should say something sweet to the baby, too."

Chuckling at her words, Harry locked eyes with his child and continued with a tender voice.

"Love has always been the only thing that saved me. Every single happiness in my life, more miraculous than any magic, was given to me by your mother."

The child gazed steadily at Harry, as if she truly understood his words.

Gently wrapping his hand around the baby's tiny, delicate fingers, Harry spoke on with a voice full of love, his eyes shimmering with tears.

"Even if the world were to end today, the one and only perfect happy ending of my life is this very moment. I've spent my whole life in the wizarding world, but... I used to think I had spent all the magic of my life the very night I first met your mother."

Harry raised his head to gaze deeply into the girl shining more brilliantly than anything else in the world, despite her exhaustion.

"But I was wrong. The true miracle is beginning right now, alongside both of you."

Harry's voice trembled softly.

"All the magic that saved me was ultimately you, and now that magic rests in my arms with two eyes that mirror ours. Thank you, my everything... I will devote the rest of my life to loving both of you forever."

"Nervous, Lily?"

To send off their beloved daughter on her very first day at Hogwarts, Harry and malfoyd stood side by side on Platform 9 ¾.

"Yeah... I'm a little worried."

"What is there to worry about, Potter?"

malfoyd said with a soft, affectionate smile, gently smoothing down her daughter's messy blonde hair.

"What if I can't make any friends there? What if I get sorted into a House and just don't fit in?"

At those words, malfoyd and Harry exchanged a fond, knowing smile, as if reminiscing about old memories that mirrored this very moment.

Harry knelt down on one knee, holding back his overwhelming emotions as he met his child's clear, emerald-green eyes.

"Lily. Hogwarts, and this wide world out there, are filled with so many different people. Among them, you'll find people whose hearts click perfectly with yours, and others who might rub you the wrong way at first."

Gently stroking the sweet girl's cheek, Harry continued with a sincere voice.

"But just because someone doesn't seem to get along with you right now, it doesn't mean they're someone who will never understand you. People's bonds are truly magical things... Always keep that in mind."

"Really? Even if we don't get along at first... can we still become true friends?"

"Of course. Your mum and I didn't get along at all when we first met. In fact, calling it 'not getting along' is an understatement—we were practically sworn enemies."

Hearing a story about her mum and dad's past that she had never heard before, Lily's eyes widened in pure curiosity as she looked back and forth between them.

malfoyd let out a soft snort of laughter, playfully nudging Harry's shoulder before taking over.

"That's right. Your dad was an absolute, hopeless idiot back then~"

"I was just utterly blinded because your mum shone way too brightly, that's all. And your mum was the cutest, most stubborn little menace in the entire world."

At their banter, Lily burst into a fit of giggles. Right then, the Hogwarts Express let out a grand, roaring whistle to signal its departure.

Hurryingly scrambling up onto the train steps, Lily waved regretfully at her mum and dad. Just before the train moved, Harry stepped right up to the threshold and firmly grasped her tiny hand, locking eyes with her.

"Lily, never, ever forget this. You are the most brilliant treasure of ours, born by overcoming the harsh odds and miraculous destiny that the whole world said was impossible."

malfoyd wiped away a hint of hidden, teary emotion and gently stroked the back of Lily's hand.

"You carry your dad's recklessly burning courage and your mum's unshakeable ambition, all wrapped into one. There is nothing in this world to be afraid of. And no matter what happens, always remember that there are two people standing right behind you who will love and support you until the very end."

At that warm, deeply magical promise, Lily wiped away her tears as if she wasn't scared anymore, flashing them a bright, confident smile.

The train carrying their child slowly began to glide away from the platform.

Leaning naturally into Harry's embrace, malfoyd waved goodbye to the receding train and chuckled softly.

"Look at her, Potter. That child's eyes truly hold everything about the two of us."

Harry pulled his brilliantly glowing wife tightly against his side, pressing his lips gently against her radiant smile—a smile he had cherished all his life.

"The greatest magic of my life was meeting you that day... but right now, our tomorrow that you and this child are going to build together is my truly eternal miracle."

"You know how many points we'll lose if we get caught doing this here, Potter?"

malfoyd's breathless reprimand carried a much more dizzying temptation than any warning.

"You're one to talk, after casting spells with your eyes at me the whole time during class. To be honest, I was going out of my mind trying to hold back."

The moment Harry replied, he dove deep and passionately into her lips. At the breathless kiss, malfoyd's pale neck flushed crimson in an instant. As Harry's hands wrapped around her slender, delicate waist, his heart gave a sudden, heavy thump. The touch of her body—so much smaller and more fragile than his own—was transmitted directly to his fingertips.

malfoyd let out a half-hearted huff as if she hated it, but her hazy vision was already filled solely with Harry's deep, burning gaze, as though he had completely lost his reason. Amidst her ragged breath, she barely managed to squeeze out a voice.

"Hnh... Take it slow. Don't rush into it..."

Chuckling softly at her words, Harry leaned close and whispered low against her ear, as if asking for permission.

"I'll take it slow, exactly like you said."

Harry carefully slid his hand underneath her soft knit sweater and shirt. The moment his touch, previously chilled by the autumn air, brushed against the hot, tender bare skin beneath her clothes, a tiny gasp she couldn't swallow slipped past malfoyd's lips.

"But I don't think I can wait because I'm too impatient."

Amidst the darkness enveloping them, only the faint murmurs of Hogwarts served as their sole background music. Harry held her shoulders tightly, embracing her soft warmth entirely, as if handling the most precious and fragile treasure in the world.

malfoyd closed her eyes tightly, her fingers clutching frantically at Harry's broad shoulders. Gone was any trace of their prickly, bitter rivalry from the past; the space was filled solely with an uncontrollable thirst and sweet heat drawing them toward one another.

"Potter... you really are impossible..."

Her voice, whispering out a reproach, was already trembling, and charmed by her reaction, Harry smiled sweetly and pressed his lips to hers once more in a burning kiss. Within the cold stone walls of Hogwarts, it was the moment their shared warmth flared up brighter and hotter than ever.

malfoyd tried faintly to push against Harry's chest with her cheeks burning red, but all the strength had already drained from her limp grip.

"If I had known you were this fragile from the very beginning, I wouldn't have wasted all those years fighting with you."

Every time Harry's touch traced smooth lines upward along her waist beneath her sweater, malfoyd's breath grew noticeably shallower. Every brush of his warm palm against the skin exposed to the cool draft sent a thrilling shiver coursing through her whole body.

Unable to hold back any longer, malfoyd wrapped both arms around Harry's neck and buried her face against his shoulder. Harry couldn't resist pressing another gentle kiss against the white, delicate nape of her neck exposed amidst her disheveled blonde hair.

"Potter... you really are a bad guy..."

"I'll take that as a compliment."

With a low, amused chuckle, Harry's hands began carefully unbuttoning her shirt, one by one. The secret, stone-walled alcove was filled entirely with the sound of their ragged breaths and skin pressing against skin.

Neither the gaze of the world nor the rules of the house mattered to either of them in this moment. As if their mutual warmth were the only true law and reality, Harry pulled her even deeper into his embrace, surrendering completely to a sweet, unstoppable temptation.

The very last button of her white shirt slipped free, leaving their bare skin to press flush against the cool draft of the stone walls.

Overwhelmed by a surging wave of emotion and shyness, malfoyd clamped her eyes shut and grabbed tightly onto Harry's broad shoulders, her fingernails pressing deep.

"Hah... Potter, wait..."

"You're far too pretty for me to stop now."

Harry's low, husky voice tickled her ear. Trapped between the inescapable, cold stonework and Harry's scorching heat caging her in, malfoyd felt entirely dizzy, losing all sense of reason.

Each time Harry's lips drifted softly down her collarbone, a sweet sigh mingled with a muffled moan escaped her lips. The sensation of her much smaller, fragile body melting and intertwining completely within his arms made Harry feel as though his last thread of reason had snapped.

"Nhn... Seriously... I'm going to make you pay for this later..."

"Alright, I'll take all of it, so feel free to blame me as much as you want."

Without a moment's hesitation, their breathing fused into one complete rhythm.

What filled the secret room was no longer the chilly night air of Hogwarts, but only the heavy breathing and sticky heat born from their mutual indulgence. In a spell far more powerful and sweet than any magic in the world, they lost track of time itself, sinking deeper and deeper into each other's warmth.

Harry Potter survived his death and became the boy who lived. Dracaena, survived hers after Sectumsempra.

Harry horrified and sorry of what he did, gave her a pin like his scar, these clips are nothing special, really.... theyre just simple little things, bent into a zigzag like the scar on his forehead.

But perhaps, that was enough.

They held her beautiful hair gently. Her face, visible again, the way it once was when they were young. That exhausted yet still so regal, still so beautiful face. His heart feels like its gonna jump out of his chest. And her slightly peeking forehead, did he forgot to mention that he had found it cute ever since they were young?

They are a reminder of what he almost did to the one he loves.

He hopes she wears it. He realized he is scared. He hopes she accepts it. His hands are trembling.

He was a wizard, but there are some things even magic cannot simply undo. So, all he can only do is pray. His feet is cold. He prays that she forgives him for what he has done. Pray that in the future, she... He cant feel his knees.

Maybe that gift was a symbol, maybe a contract, a prayer, something that matches his scar on his forehead, also maybe a spell, or perhaps, simply, just a promise, to her, or to himself, to treasure and protect.

The girl who loved.

The Pensieve and The Resentment

Harry pulled his head out of the Pensieve, dazed. What he had just seen was a new and enormous piece in the Dark Lord’s puzzle, the Horcruxes, and understanding it fully would have demanded all his attention. But he couldn’t give it. The duel with Dracaena was still lodged in his mind.

Inside, he wanted to scream at himself, to convince himself that she’d had it coming. She had treated him worse than ever this year: she had left him petrified on the train, kicked him in the face, and mocked him by wishing him a lovely time in London. Then she had tried to hurt Dumbledore in the most twisted ways: with the cursed necklace that nearly killed Katie Bell, with the poisoned mead that nearly killed Ron. And she had confirmed to his face that she was a Death Eater, for God’s sake!

And yet his conscience wouldn’t settle. He had gotten rid of the Half-Blood Princess’s book, but he couldn’t forget what he had done with his anger. He couldn’t forgive himself for the marks on that sulky, doll-like face. And above all, he couldn’t imagine a future in which she forgave him and they took up again the twisting, waterlogged paths of that strange friendship they had barely begun to walk.

Harry kept drowning in those thoughts while a weary Dumbledore tried to explain what they had just learned about Voldemort. But the boy’s distraction did not escape the old headmaster.

“Harry? I understand that this year Hogwarts hasn’t been entirely kind to you. Though it never has been, has it? Not to you, at least.”

“Sir...” Harry choked back the answer before his voice could break, but he couldn’t choke back the sorrow in his watering eyes.

“Ah, yes. The falling-out with Miss Malfoy is beginning to weigh on you. I’m aware of the details. And postponing this conversation would only be counterproductive; of that I’m aware as well. You must understand, Harry, that every negative feeling plays into the Dark Lord’s hands. If you wish to defeat him someday, you will have to cleanse your heart of any resentment toward Dracaena.

“And even without Voldemort’s shadow over us, allow me to counsel you as an old friend: rarely do we cross paths with the right person. Miss Malfoy has everything necessary for the two of you to be happy at each other’s side. She simply hides it beneath tons of pride, imposed by others and by herself. Don’t let the Dark Lord rob you of the chance to see her smile at you. Even if she has been cruel to you, remember that he is twisted enough to toy with people’s minds and speak through their lips.”

“Thank you, Professor... But what if the resentment I hold isn’t toward her, but toward myself?”

“Then the form changes, but not the substance. Your duty remains to reconcile that unique affection, painful and yet so precious, that the two of you shared. Perhaps you must first learn to forgive yourself, but that is an advantage: if you already acknowledge your guilt, you can take the first step, ask forgiveness from the depths of your soul, and give her time to do the same. Now come. A hard task awaits us.”

Dumbledore studied him a moment longer than he needed to, like someone confirming that a piece fits.

“Yes, sir. Thank you very much.”

Harry steeled himself for the next challenge. With a clear mind and a bandaged heart, he closed his eyes and exhaled.

Dracaena drew in a great gulp of air, thick with the aroma of potions and starched sheets, and shot upright. She tried to open her eyes, but one of them throbbed fiercely. She sucked a breath through her teeth, her face twisted in a grimace, and raised a hand to her face. Her fingertips confirmed it: her right eye was bandaged. Her whole body felt heavy, as if she were surfacing from a long fever.

A woman’s voice reached her from a corner draped in shadow:

“So you finally deign to wake, Miss Malfoy. For two days you have been resting in this infirmary while the rest of us clean up your messes. Have you lost the will to carry out the Dark Lord’s designs? Is your family’s standing worth so little to you?”

The clouds parted, and moonlight spilled through the window, sketching out the stern face of Professor Snape. Her eyes were harder than usual, like those of someone carrying worry and anger in equal measure.

Dracaena managed only a murmur:

“Why...?”

Snape cut her off with the speed of a lightning strike:

“Why are you still alive? I couldn’t say. Perhaps because my life depends on yours?” She paused, as though on the verge of saying something more, and buried it beneath another remark. “And be grateful, besides, that Potter was weak enough not to finish you off.”

“Impossible... He hates me...” the girl replied.

“I couldn’t care less.”

The reply was so theatrical that anyone who wasn’t shattered inside would have heard the lie in it. It was almost as if Snape were forcing herself to be cruel. She finished:

“We act in a few hours. I suggest you feed those negative feelings; you will need them to complete your task. I also suggest you leave your doubts in this room. And I suggest you be punctual. I will be waiting at the entrance to the Astronomy Tower.”

She rose and strode toward the door.

Dracaena clenched the sheets in her fists. Unable to lift her face, she began to sob, tears running down from her good eye as the gauze over the other bloomed red.

First batch of Goblet of Fire is done - condensing the original work's start down to get to the actual plot that people care about! Chapters 1-6 of the original, which were about 30k words, are now condensed to a prologue and two chapters of 13k words total. Its a bit tedious, but doing rewrites like this means that I won't have to do any summaries or have to worry about copyrighted prose on AO3. I'm also now less beholden to matching Rowling's original prose and can just write the scenes out how I think best.

Anyway, now I can actually start on the Draconia specific stuff!

I've divided the book up into 5 parts, I'm thinking I'll release each part as its completed. The parts are:
- The Triwizard Tournament, which covers the prologue, World Cup, return to Hogwarts, arrival of Beauxbatons and Durmstrang, and Harry's unexpected selection as the fourth champion.
- The First Task, which covers Harry's decision to compete, his growing friendship with Draconia, preparation for the dragons, and the First Task itself.
- The Yule Ball, which covers Harry and Draconia's developing romance, their misunderstandings, the Yule Ball, and a special Christmas at Malfoy Manor.
- The Second Task, which covers the golden egg mystery, Harry's underwater preparations, the Black Lake, and the growing mystery surrounding the Tournament.
- The Third Task, which covers Harry's final preparations for the tournament up to the end.

I want to say a weekly release schedule for these, but I won't make promises I don't know I can keep. What I will say is to expect quite a lot of Draconia in this book!

2113096756380500022:
Dracaena threw herself into the duty that had been laid upon her. There was no turning back: she had opened the gates of Hogwarts to the Dark Lord’s Death Eaters, and from that moment the gears of evil turned without resistance toward the fulfillment of her obligations.

What tipped the balance toward darkness was the confusion of a manipulated girl, convinced that stopping to face the consequences of her mistakes would never be enough to earn the forgiveness of the one she admired most. She felt unwanted, despised and, above all, hated. From the start of the year, it had been imperative for her to feed and root those murky feelings deep within her being; only then did she believe herself capable of guaranteeing her family’s survival.

Professor Snape was waiting at the entrance to the Astronomy Tower, to one side of the doorway, arms crossed, her expression indifferent. Without looking at her or saying a word, she jerked her head toward the staircase and returned it to its place, as if to say, go on, climb.

Before the first step, one of those that climbed toward a full stop and a new paragraph in her life, Dracaena couldn’t help but falter. Driven by that same contempt, she gripped her wand with all her strength, drew a breath and, eyes fixed above, set off on her left foot, off on the wrong foot. She did not notice. Her mind, which she could no longer govern, retraced, step by step, how her thoughts had mutated since the Dark Lord had handed her this task:

Should I talk to Potter about it?

Potter wouldn’t understand.

Potter doesn’t want me near him.

Potter is to blame for all of this.

Potter is my enemy.

Potter hates me.

All her rage gathered in her jaw, clenched in a snarl, and she hissed through her teeth:

“Potter, Potter, Potter...”

Then, from some corner of her soul, an inner voice stopped her cold, a few steps from the top, heavy with a different kind of negative feeling: anguish.

Harry hates us...

She couldn’t move. Her pupils shrank to almost nothing and her mind went blank, as if something in the deepest part of her were trying to hold her back.

Then, from above, Dumbledore’s weary voice pulled her out of the trance. It was only a whisper, as if he were speaking in secret to someone else:

“...Trust me.”

She raised her eyes again. Doubt was wearing away at her resolve; even so, she chose to wield it, and climbed the last steps.

The Goblet of Fire, Part 1, is now complete! Links below!

As I have mentioned before, this work represents a COMPLETE retelling of Goblet of Fire - no summaries, no edits of the original prose, only referencing when needed. This is because Draconia Malfoy is now affecting the story so thoroughly that editing would be more effort than it is worth, and there is practically not a single event that goes unchanged thanks to her presence.

Book four will have a lot more romantic content than the previous edits - as expected, with the Yule Ball coming up. It also introduces a few of my own changes to canon events to tell the story I want to, though this early not many are visible.

Part 1 weighs in at about 50k words, and is one of the longer parts, covering events up until right before the arrival of Beauxbatons and Durmstrang. Future parts, save for the final, should be shorter and therefore released more quickly.

Part 2 will cover the first task, Part 3 the Yule Ball, Part 4 the second task, and Part 5 the final task.

I hope you enjoy reading! This is a significant undertaking, so I greatly appreciate your words of support and efforts to share the project around.

A reminder to all the Yearners in the Malfoid tag.... 

While the algorithm does plot against things trending for long times... what you can do to help combat that is remember to interact with the posts you like.   I know that it's easy to fall into the habit of just clicking likes and reshares, but this actually doesn't promote the spreading of content beyond a certain reach... and certainly not after they've started throttling the tag.

Leave a comment on art you like or reshare, even if its just simply to say why you like it.  Engage in discussions of story snippets and rewrites.  Not only does this help with getting content seen more broadly (The algorithm favors engagement), it also bolsters and encourages those creators to keep making content (Yes, egos must be fed).

So, if you like a particular artist or piece of art, remember to engage with it!

2117013828408086683:
The Tower

Harry reached the top of the great rock lashed by the waves outside the sea cave, holding up a poisoned Dumbledore. The old man was pale, weak and lost, his mind clouded. The boy had never seen him like this. To him, Dumbledore was the greatest pillar of Hogwarts: he felt that his corner of the wizarding world was safe because of him, perhaps even the whole world. Neither last year’s quarrels nor the flaws he had learned to see in him this term had dimmed his admiration for his mentor, his general in the war against the evil that Voldemort embodied. Seeing that pillar cracked and swaying filled him with unease.

“Sir, we have to go straight to the hospital wing. Madam Pomfrey...”

“No,” Dumbledore interrupted. “Severa Snape... I will take us to the top of the Astronomy Tower, Harry. Go straight to her, wake her, tell her what happened, and speak to no one else.”

Harry hesitated. He had never trusted Snape, and the state Dumbledore was in stirred a hunch he couldn’t decipher. But he didn’t dare defy the headmaster, and he no longer had the Felix Felicis as an excuse to disobey.

“Yes, sir!”

They appeared at the top of the tower, just as the old wizard had said they would. Even poisoned, he remained the only wizard able to Apparate inside Hogwarts. While Harry helped him settle against a bench so he could wait a little more comfortably for Professor Snape, both of them watched, mouths agape, as the Dark Mark rose into the sky above the castle.

“Sir, take cover! I’ll go for Snape as fast as I can, she’ll know what to...”

“No,” the old man cut in again. “Harry, someone is coming. Go down the back stairs and hide on the floor below. Do nothing. Whatever happens, do not show yourself, and return to your dormitory as soon as you can, speaking to no one.”

Dumbledore saw the hesitation in the boy’s stance and hurried to cut it short:

“Do as I ask. Trust me, my dear boy... Trust me.”

He said it with a sweetness so precise that Harry couldn’t tell whether it was a plea or a calculation. He chose to believe it was the latter: that the old man had everything under control.

Harry nodded and slipped down, quick and silent. He looked for a spot from which he could see the intruder, but all he could make out was his mentor, struggling mightily to hide his pain and weakness. He heard footsteps. He saw Dumbledore mask a flicker of surprise in his eyes and greet the newcomer with feigned calm:

“Good evening, Dracaena.”

The girl took a few steps toward Dumbledore, and the moonlight revealed the scars that crossed her face, the eye bandaged with blood-stained gauze, and trembling hands gripping a wand in a threatening stance. A hollow opened in Harry’s chest.

Every mark bore his name. The anguish it stirred in him was hard to describe, and all he could do was pray that she hadn’t come here to do something rash, and that Dumbledore had strength enough to put a stop to this without being too harsh with her.

Like a distant echo, the old man’s voice pulled him back to the scene:

“And what brings you here on such a lovely spring night?”

The Goblet of Fire, Part 2, is now complete! Links below!
This part covers the First Task, with Draconia's presence increasingly influencing how I plot the story.

I did say that future parts would be shorter than Part 1. I lied, because Part 2 weighs in at approximately 69k words, bringing the book to nearly 120k so far. Oops.

Here's an out of context list of things that happen in Part 2, in no particular order!
- Harry punches Snape in the nose
- McGonagall threatens to join in
- Moody makes Harry ask Draconia for a dance
- Harry gives Draconia a pet dragon
- Harry tells Draconia he loves the way Dementors kiss

As before, this is a complete retelling of Goblet of Fire, with the relationship between Harry and Draconia becoming increasingly central to the story. Part 3 will cover the Yule Ball, where things will be getting SPICYYYY

I hope you enjoy reading! Thank you to everyone who's been following, commenting on, and sharing the project. Your support means a great deal, especially with how much work this book has become.

The Goblet of Fire, Part 3, is now complete! Links below!

As mentioned in previous posts, this is a COMPLETE retelling of Goblet of Fire, with Draconia Malfoy's presence influencing practically every aspect of the story.

Part 3 covers the events between the First Task and the Yule Ball, and represents the most significant departure from canon thus far. Much of this part is entirely original material, with a particular focus on developing the relationships between the characters. A lot of what I've been building towards throughout the previous three books finally comes to fruition here.

This is also the part of Goblet of Fire I've been most looking forward to writing, and those of you who have been following the project since Philosopher's Stone can probably imagine why.

Part 3 weighs in at approximately 48k words, bringing the book to nearly 168k words so far. Part 4 will cover the Second Task, and Part 5 will cover the Final Task and the conclusion of the book.

I hope you enjoy reading! Thank you to everyone who has been following the project, sharing it around and leaving comments. I greatly appreciate your continued support throughout what has become a considerably larger undertaking than I originally anticipated.
